Definition: Megiddon or Megiddo, a place in Palestine
BiblicalUsage: Megiddo is a city on the plain of Jezreel, named where the tribes failed to drive out the Canaanites, and where Josiah was slain by Pharaoh Necho. Zechariah says the mourning in Jerusalem will be as the mourning of Hadadrimmon in the valley of Megiddon.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Megiddo is the battlefield of the Bible: the kings fought there, the righteous king died there, and the last mourning will be like the mourning there — because the plain of Megiddo is where the wars of men keep ending, and where God's war will end.
RelatedPeople: Joshua; King Josiah; Zechariah the Prophet
